chunks: And by this chain of narration from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib. He said: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Aban, from Sallam ibn Abi 'Amra, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbudh, from Abu al-Tufayl, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said:

I heard the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) say: I am the master of the Prophets, and Ali ibn Abi Talib is the master of the Deputies, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the two masters of the youth of the people of Paradise, and the Imams after them both are the masters of the God-fearing. Our ally is the ally of God, and our enemy is the enemy of God. Obedience to us is obedience to God, and disobedience to us is disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.الْوَصِيِّينَ: Deputies/Successors — those designated by prophets to carry on their mission
key_terms.سَيِّدَا شَبَابِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ: The two masters of the youth of Paradise — a well-known prophetic title for al-Hasan and al-Husayn
key_terms.سَيِّدُ النَّبِيِّينَ: Master/Lord of the Prophets — title affirming Muhammad's supreme prophethood
key_terms.وَلِيُّ اللَّهِ: Ally/guardian of God — technical Shia theological term for those whose loyalty is synonymous with loyalty to God

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the status of Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Hasan (AS) as a direct report from the Prophet (SAWW), establishes the hierarchical spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt. The Prophet declares himself master of all Prophets and names Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and subsequent Imams as divinely appointed leaders. The culminating declaration — that loyalty to the Imams is loyalty to God — frames wilayah (guardianship) as the central pillar of Shia theology, understood by the early Muslim community in the context of the Prophet's designation of successors.
